IT guy here. I have some thoughts about all this ICANN nonsense. Quite frankly, I don't care where ICANN goes, they can go to hell for all I care. Just a little history fact, there have been several attempts by private individuals to make alternatives to ICANN, but they simply didn't have the finances or support to become mainstream enough to provide an alternative to ICANN's DNS.

"Alternative" you say?

Yes, alternative. You don't actually need to use DNS servers from your ISP, work, government, university, or ICANN itself. You can host your own DNS, or simply keep your own hosts file with a list of websites, servers, and its corresponding IP addresses. Hell, a private coalition of legit/honest DNS servers existed even before ICANN thought about going to the UN. You can tell your computer to use those servers as your DNS provider instead of your ISP, work, school, etc. Assuming you have the administrative privilege to do so.

If you are nutty enough, and well endowed with money enough, you may want to try your hand at a new DNS and get everyone on board with that. If you can promise major companies their own domains, like .coke, .nike, .toyota, etc, and have an even more secure naming system than the security vulnerability prone DNS, you may find that ICANN screams bloody murder because we technically don't need them.

So what about all this shutting off your DNS because of elitists and dictators nonsense? Well, they can already do that. As in, shut down your IP address, or simply send in a crack team of Federal agents and confiscate your shit. Don't worry about your host name no longer working. If someone powerful wants to shut you down, most every ISP, search engine, and government has the complete means of shutting you down and has had that power for over a decade.

Think it's unfair that you will lose your convenience privilege because your DNS gets whacked? Again, should your users subscribe to those legit and honest DNS servers I was talking about, you may find that your DNS records still exist on the web. ICANN cannot delete DNS records on private servers. For the rest of the average folks that can no longer frequent your site, that's on you to find alternative means to get them that DNS, or let people know you are being censored by a private party's DNS server. All the more reason for the people to replace ICANN with something underground or alternative.
